Tuesday, March 19, 2024 - 06:00 PM

The next Ordinary Meeting of the Council will be held on 19th March 2024 in the Council Chamber at the Shire Administration office– commencing at 6:00 pm (AWST) to consider and resolve on the matters set out in the attached agenda.

All meetings are open to the public, except for matters raised by Council under “Confidential Items”.

Members of the public may ask a question at an Ordinary Council meeting under “Public Question Time”.

Council Meetings

The Council meets on the third Tuesday of the month at 6:00pm in the Council Chambers located in the Administration Building 88-92 Prinsep Street Norseman WA 6443.

Items for inclusion in the agenda for the meetings will need to be received by the Shire of Dundas by the Monday of the week preceding the meeting.

Members of the public are invited and encouraged to attend Council Meetings.

Special Council Meetings, ARIC & Electors' Meetings 

Annual General Meeting of Electors

The Annual General Meeting of Electors is the meeting required to be held once every financial year for the purpose of discussing the annual report and any other general business. The meeting gives electors of the Shire the opportunity to ask questions, make statements and move motions to be voted on by the electors of the Shire. 

To register attendance and to submit a motion or question, please complete this form at least 24 hours prior to the Annual General Meeting of Electors'.

For more information about the Annual General Meeting of Electors, please refer to the fact sheet. 

Special Council Meeting

When required, a special meeting of council may be called by the President or by at least one third of the councillors. The CEO will convene the special meeting and arrange public notice if the meeting is to be open to the public. A special meeting requires that:

  • public notice be given specifying the purpose of the meeting
  • it must only deal with the items of business as set out in the notice of the meeting.

If the local government decides that the meeting is open to the public, the CEO must provide public notice of the special meeting on the local government’s website as soon as practicable after the decision to hold the meeting has been made.

Audit, Risk & Improvement Committee 

The Local Government Act 1995 (the Act) requires that all local governments establish an Audit, Risk & Improvement Committee (ARIC). An ARIC plays a key role in assisting a local government to fulfil its governance and oversight responsibilities in relation to financial reporting, internal control structure, risk management systems, legislative compliance, ethical accountability and the internal and external audit functions.

The committee shall meet at least quarterly. Additional meetings shall be convened at the discretion of the presiding person.
